title: Typhoon Champi Brings Storms and a Day Off in Taiwan
summary:
A strong storm called Typhoon Champi came close to Taiwan on Friday. A typhoon is a powerful storm in this part of the Pacific Ocean, like a hurricane.

Hundreds of flights in East Asia were cancelled. Officials said one person died after being swept away by waves, and 171 people were hurt. About 1,000 people left their homes to stay safe.

Earlier this week, Champi was the strongest storm on Earth so far this year, with winds of 185 miles per hour. It later got weaker.

Forecasters expected the center of the storm to pass by without hitting land in Taiwan, but they were not completely sure. Heavy rain was expected until Saturday evening.

Schools and offices closed in almost all of Taiwan. People call this a "typhoon holiday." In Japan's Okinawa, about 8,400 homes lost power.

Experts say an unusually strong El Niño, a natural warming of the Pacific Ocean, is causing many storms this year.
why_it_matters: Knowing how storms work and listening to weather warnings helps families stay safe.
